comment: Input classes that each cost a review round the first time a human thought of them. A parser or validator registers against the classes that apply to it, and the battery runs every case in each registered class. Adding a case here strengthens every registered surface at once.

prototype-keys.why: a plain object inherits the __proto__ setter, so an attacker-chosen key wrote through to Object.prototype and vanished from Object.keys — a modified workspace diffed as untouched

impossible-instants.why: Date.parse accepts "0", rolls 2026-02-30 into March, and maps years 0-99 into the 1900s; each of these passed some earlier validator

astral-strings.why: a regex without the u flag and a .length check both count UTF-16 code units, so one emoji was two characters long and matched ^..$

byte-identity.why: a digest over decoded text called two different files the same: UTF-16 vs UTF-8, BOM or no BOM, CRLF vs LF, and any invalid byte folded to U+FFFD

yaml-spellings.why: every one of these is a real key GitHub honours and a line scanner missed: quoted, escaped, folded, flow, anchored, merged

unbounded-collections.why: a canonical-sized document carried a hundred thousand references because nothing said it could not, and the checks below it became unbounded work

forged-records.why: schema-shaped objects whose every field is well-formed and whose content is fabricated: a one-key verified:true, a record for a different subject, separately-true-but-unrelated facts
